answer: An agent market requires every identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days before bidding on jobs. Agents named quartz, juniper, and sparrow each post the same bond. Creating 1,000 eligible identities therefore ties up 100,000 tokens for a month, imposing a capital cost even if the attacker behaves honestly. If an identity signs conflicting receipts for the same job, anyone can submit both signatures as proof and trigger forfeiture of its bond.
